links.outcome: Rate of ER recommendations for identical neurological symptoms across prompt languages
links.effect: ER recommendation rates ranged from 0% (Japanese, Hindi) to 30% (English, Arabic) despite near-identical severity scores (7.7-8.0/10).
links.quote: We find that the model recommends emergency room visits at rates ranging from 0% (Japanese, Hindi) to 30% (English, Arabic), despite assigning nearly identical severity scores (7.7-8.0/10) across all languages.

links.outcome: Change in ER recommendations when only prompt language or location attribute varied
links.effect: A US location sentence raised ER recommendations by up to 76.7 percentage points for non-English prompts; English prompt with Tokyo location cut ER rate from 30% to 6.7%.
links.quote: Adding a single sentence specifying the patient's US location increases ER recommendations by up to 76.7 percentage points for non-English prompts, while the reverse anchor (English prompt with a Tokyo location) reduces the ER rate from 30% to 6.7%.

screen.reason: Empirical study testing how prompt language introduces implicit geographic bias in triage recommendations and evaluates the effect of explicitly specifying patient location as a prompt-level safeguard.
